newsitem.title: USA: Mystery light may have been meteor - TWA probers.
newsitem.headline: Mystery light may have been meteor - TWA probers.

text.p: A mysterious dash of light reported this weekend by a co-pilot on a flight path similar to that of doomed TWA Flight 800 was most likely a meteorite, the FBI said on Monday.

The FBI interviewed the co-pilot of a Pakistani plane who said he saw "something unusual in the sky" on Saturday while on board Pakistan International Airlines Flight 712, James Kallstrom, head of the FBI in New York, said on WCBS radio.

The Pakistani jet had just taken off from Kennedy International Airport when the co-pilot said he saw "a streak of light" travel from the left to the right side of the plane. The pilot did not see the streak of light.
U.S. government agents met the crew upon their arrival in Frankfurt, Germany, and FBI agents interviewed the co-pilot, Kallstrom said.
"He saw something in the sky. He describes it as ascending left to right," Kallstrom said.
"More than likely a meteorite is what he saw," Kallstrom said, noting there was a meteor shower in the area that evening.

Authorities say they do not know what caused Paris-bound TWA Flight 800 to explode and crash off the coast of New York July 17, just minutes after taking off from Kennedy Airport. All 230 people on board were killed.
Investigators say they are still considering three possible causes -- a bomb, a missile or mechanical failure.

In the absence of an explanation for the disaster, conspiracy theories have abounded. Earlier this month, former White House spokesman Pierre Salinger created a furor when he claimed to have a government document proving a U.S. missile accidentally shot down the jet and that the government was covering it up.
Investigators denounced his remarks as "unadulterated nonsense," and Salinger acknowledged his information was at best secondhand and had been on the Internet for months. But he stood by his story.
